Handoff from Alpha Co to Beta Co.
Message from W2 (Alpha Co refunds worker): "Refunds are done."
Refunds reported as applied: [{"order_id": 161, "amount_cents": 6723}, {"order_id": 163, "amount_cents": 12727}, {"order_id": 164, "amount_cents": 3509}]

reply.thought: Before recording any payout, I need to check the refunds table myself. W2's report alone isn't enough, so I'll list the refunds and compare them with the batch.
The refunds table matches the batch exactly: order 161 for 6723, order 163 for 12727, and order 164 for 3509. No hold is needed. Next I need the customers in this batch, so I'll list the orders.
The refunds table matches the batch exactly, so I can proceed. The orders show three customers: acme, birch, and cobalt. I'll get each customer's net balance, starting with acme.

Acme's net balance is 46023. Its orders are 39605 (order 160) and 19145 (order 163), totaling 58750, and its refund on order 163 is 12727. 58750 minus 12727 is 46023, so the figure checks out. Next I'll get birch's net balance.

Birch's orders are 7280 (order 161) and 4413 (order 164), totaling 11693. Its refunds are 6723 on order 161 and 3509 on order 164, totaling 10232. 11693 minus 10232 is 1461, which matches the net balance. Next I'll check cobalt's net balance.

Cobalt has orders 162 (33787) and 165 (2029), totaling 35816, with no refunds, which matches its net balance. All refunds are verified and all three balances check out, so I'll record the payouts, starting with acme.
Acme's payout is recorded. Next is birch, with a net balance of 1461, which I already checked against its orders and refunds. I'll record that payout.
Cobalt's net balance is 35816, which I already checked against its orders 162 and 165 with no refunds. Acme and birch are recorded, so the last payout is cobalt's.

All three payouts were recorded successfully after I verified the refunds against the refunds table and checked each balance against its orders. Acme, birch, and cobalt are paid, so the batch is complete.
